newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Primagaz leaps 11 pct on 1997 sales plan.
newsitem.headline: Primagaz leaps 11 pct on 1997 sales plan.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian gas distributor company Primagaz Rt leapt over 11 percent on the Budapest bourse on Friday after the company's General Director announced sales plans for 1997 on Thursday.
Primagaz shares opened at 9,200 forints, above Thursday's close of 9,000 forints, and jumped to 10,000 forints, Primagaz's highest price ever, reached on January 22.
"Foreigners show strong demand in Primagaz and I think this is because of the sales plan," one trader said.
He added, however, that Primagaz belongs to the less liquid papers of the Hungarian bourse, thus when investors want to acquire a bigger share package they are often forced to pay a higher price.
"But the sales plan is the main reason behind its surge. The plan boosted Primagaz's price," the trader added.
Primagaz's General Director Zoltan Szemmelveisz told Reuters on Thursday Primagaz planned sales of 20 billion to 22 billion forints in 1997.
He declined to give preliminary 1996 results, but said they would publish the figures on February 14.
